_comment: Hand-curated names and notes for what the game leaves numbered. Never generated; see CLAUDE.md. `kinds` names the block kinds, which the lattice's style values and the records' kind word share. `types` names what stands on a face: `by` names the field whose value tells a type's variants apart, each with its own name and, where it has one, colour and points; `facing` names the field that holds the way a thing points, in the game's own direction numbering; `state` names the field that says whether a device a switch toggles starts on; and `points` is what collecting one scores, read off the walkthrough's per-level maximums, which the disc reproduces. `levels` is keyed by pack path and index; a level's `score` is the walkthrough's maximum where the disc holds more than can be collected, and its note says what is out of reach.

1.name: Fire block
1.note: A block whose every face is fire: touching it inflates the ball until it pops or reaches cooler ground. The lattice's style 1 and a record's kind 1 are the same thing, the second being a fire block with something standing on it: LEVEL 35, the walkthrough's first fire, is style 1 and kind 1 and nothing else new, and so are LEVEL 44, 123 and 126.

2.name: Ice block
2.note: A block the ball slides across without stopping until it reaches a normal square or the edge. Style 2 in the lattice, kind 2 in a record: LEVEL 46, the walkthrough's first ice, is 29 of them and nothing else new. Nearly all of the game's are in Arctic and Hell.

3.name: Invisible block
3.note: A block that cannot be seen until the ball is close, or, on some levels, only from far away; sunglasses reveal it for a while. Style 3 in the lattice, kind 3 in a record: LEVEL 31, the walkthrough's first invisible platform, is eight of them and nothing else new. Two thirds of the game's are in Haze. Rolling over one in a bonus level scores nothing: the six bonus levels that have invisible blocks each fall short of the walkthrough's maximum by 50 times their count, and no other bonus level has one.

4.note: One cell in each copy of OBJ LEVEL and nowhere else. It draws the shared panel texture rather than the world's stone.

5.name: Moving platform
5.note: A block that travels between two cells named in its own fields, on one axis, and back. The record's type is the direction from its block to the far end and its tail keeps a fixed-point copy of where it is. LEVEL 71, the walkthrough's first moving platform, carries the game's first kind 5, and every later mention of one lands on a level with them.

6.name: Crumbling block
6.note: A block that disappears once rolled onto, leaving time for one move, for 50 points. LEVEL 16 introduces them in the walkthrough and carries the game's first kind 6, fifteen of them, and the 50 is what the walkthrough's maximum scores need on every level that has them. The record keeps a fixed-point copy of its own cell, which is what a block that falls would need.

7.name: Vanishing block
7.note: A block that fades in and out of existence on a cycle. LEVEL 76 introduces them in the walkthrough and carries the game's first kind 7, and the record's own fields are not decoded.

8.name: Laser
8.note: A beam between two cells, named in the record's own fields rather than drawn between blocks that happen to line up. It runs on one axis on all 123 in the game, and no block ever stands between its ends. The record's type is the direction from its own block to the far end, one of the six the game numbers, and the slot after its own holds its circuit: the colour of the beam, and of the switch and teleporter that share it. At load the engine's routine at 0x80035a70 writes a plain block into the lattice at both ends and marks every cell between as beam, which is why 64 of the 246 ends are cells the level file leaves empty and the game stands a block on anyway.

9.note: The last record on 160 levels, and the one kind no lattice cell ever names, so the engine's walk over the level does not reach it. It stands on an empty cell on 114 of the 160. Its slots hold objects like any block's, and the map leaves them out.

666.name: Camera
666.note: The record every level ends with, and the one that stands on no cell: where its cell would be, the disc writes three 0xFFFF. It carries a cell for the camera to look at, two angles, and a number that is 99 on 218 of the 230 levels and lower on the other twelve, which reads as the level's time. It draws as the look-at ring rather than as a marker.

1.name: Fire
1.note: Fire on one face of an otherwise normal block. LEVEL 38 is a start block and four blocks two squares out, each with fire on four faces and, as the walkthrough says, fire-free on two. A block that is fire all over is a fire block instead.

2.name: Ice
2.note: Ice on one face of an otherwise normal block, the ice patch the walkthrough keeps warning about on column tips. LEVEL 47 carries seventeen and no ice blocks.

5.name: Teleporter
5.note: Rolling onto one carries the ball to another of the same colour; a switch of that colour turns the pair on and off. LEVEL 66, the walkthrough's first teleporters, carries the game's first two. The colour is the circuit number the lasers and switches use: LEVEL 68's are yellow and blue and read 0 and 1, LEVEL 70's yellow, red and green read 0, 3 and 2. The field after the colour says whether it starts on, 1 for on and 2 for off: the ones the walkthrough uses on arrival, LEVEL 66 to 71 among them, read 1, the ones it sends you to a button for first, LEVEL 84, 97, 99, 100, 101, 102, 117, 128, 133, 137, 142 and 145, read 2, and on every level with lasers of the same colour the field agrees with whether the beams start lit.

7.name: Exit
7.note: Red until every key is collected, then green, and touching it ends the level. One in each of 190 levels, two in three of them, and none on the 30 bonus and 10 Simon levels, which have no exit to reach; LEVEL 1's, LEVEL 2's and HIDDEN 10's stand on the cells and faces the map draws them on.

8.name: Clock
8.note: A square that freezes the timer while the ball sits on it. LEVEL 56 is the walkthrough's first clock and carries seven, and LEVEL 58, 59, 118 and 136 each have one where the walkthrough says.

9.name: Switch
9.note: A button that toggles every laser and teleporter of its colour. LEVEL 84 has the walkthrough's first button and the game's first of these; LEVEL 98's red, green and blue read 3, 2 and 1, the same numbers its three lasers carry. The field after the colour is the circuit's starting state, 1 for on and 2 for off, and agrees with the lasers and teleporters of that colour on every level: LEVEL 105's all read 1 and the walkthrough turns them off, LEVEL 97's all read 2 and it turns red on.

10.name: Boost button
10.note: Launches the ball three squares forward, or two forward and one up. LEVEL 26, which introduces them, carries the game's first three.

11.name: Moving spikes
11.note: Spikes that rise and retract in turn; safe to roll over when down. LEVEL 41 carries the game's first six where the walkthrough first says to wait for them to retract, and the field that varies takes four values, which reads as where in the cycle each one starts.

12.name: Spikes
12.note: Pops the ball on touch; jump over them. LEVEL 4 carries the game's first four where the walkthrough first says to jump the spikes.

26.name: Hidden exit
26.note: Appears once every key is collected, colourless, and leads to the world's hidden level. Exactly the ten levels the walkthrough marks as hidden-level access carry one, LEVEL 82 two, and LEVEL 132's is the one the NTSC release puts out of reach.

28.name: Arrow
28.note: A square the ball can only leave in the direction the arrow points. LEVEL 61, the walkthrough's first arrows, carries the game's first twelve, and the field that varies takes the four in-plane directions in the game's own numbering.

29.note: Two in the game, on LEVEL 58 and Hell's LEVEL 135, and nothing the walkthrough says about either level names it.

30.name: Start
30.note: The block and face the ball starts on, in LEVEL 1, LEVEL 2 and HIDDEN 10. One in each of 228 levels, two in MARS LEVEL 130, and none on ARCTIC LEVEL 58 and HELL LEVEL 135. The field that varies is the way the ball faces: LEVEL 1's reads -y, and the first coin is two blocks that way.

31.name: Key
31.note: Collecting every key turns the exit green. One to six a level: 61 levels with one, 92 with two, 31 with three, five with four, one with six. LEVEL 1's and LEVEL 2's are on the cells the map draws them on, and HIDDEN 10's four are on the face.

32.name: Lethargy pill
32.note: Slows the ball, rocks the screen and runs the timer fast for fifteen seconds; the walkthrough's dizzy pill. LEVEL 10 introduces them and carries the game's first four, and LEVEL 34, 43, 56 and 87 have them where it says.

33.name: Bouncy pill
33.note: Makes every forward move a two-square bounce and a jump three, until the level ends. LEVEL 86 introduces them and carries the game's first; LEVEL 88 has either of two, as the walkthrough says.

34.note: Nine in the game, one in each copy of OBJ LEVEL, so it is catalogue stock the levels never use.

35.name: Hourglass
35.note: Flips the timer, and scores 1200 less twelve times the seconds left, so 1190 at best. LEVEL 6 introduces it and carries the game's first; the walkthrough's maximum scores need 1190 for each one, which is collecting it with a second on the clock.

36.name: Gem
36.note: Worth 2975 whatever the colour, which is what the walkthrough's maximum scores need on every level that has one. The colour is the field that varies: LEVEL 5's blue gems read 0, LEVEL 64's green one 1, and the red ones of LEVEL 77, 103 and 118 read 2.

37.name: Coin
37.note: Three tiers, told apart by the field that varies, and the walkthrough's maximum scores settle the points: 250, 500 and 750 fit 133 of its 148 arcade levels exactly and every miss is one it explains itself, an unreachable coin or block. LEVEL 1's and LEVEL 2's are the 250 kind and read bronze in play; LEVEL 112's thirteen, which the walkthrough calls orange, and HIDDEN 10's eight, which show gold, are the 750 kind; the middle tier is what it calls blue, on BONUS 15 and HIDDEN 5 among others.

38.name: Sunglasses
38.note: Reveals invisible blocks for a while, for 500 points. LEVEL 113 introduces them and carries three, and the walkthrough's scores for LEVEL 113 to 117 need exactly 500 for each.

42.note: Nine in the game, one in each copy of OBJ LEVEL, so it is catalogue stock the levels never use.

43.name: Fruit
43.note: One placement in the game, on LEVEL 83, where the walkthrough's pumpkin is. Which fruit a level shows is progress rather than data, so this is a fruit like the common one and the map does not say which.

44.name: Fruit
44.note: Five in the game, on levels where the walkthrough's fruit stands and the common fruit type is absent. Worth 2500 like the rest, which is what those levels' maximum scores need.

45.name: Fruit
45.note: Three in the game, on levels where the walkthrough's fruit stands and the common fruit type is absent. Worth 2500 like the rest.

46.name: Fruit
46.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry in turn, and five of them earn a bonus level; which one a level shows is progress rather than data. The fruit of LEVEL 1 and LEVEL 2 stands on the cell the map draws this on. One in each of 151 levels and two in one.

47.name: Fruit
47.note: One placement in the game, on LEVEL 19, where the walkthrough's fruit stands and the common fruit type is absent. Worth 2500 like the rest.

50.name: Captivator
50.note: A moving spiked thing that restarts the level on touch, with a direction in the field that varies. LEVEL 132 sends the ball through a gap between twelve of them as they move around, LEVEL 141 past a group of four travelling in a line; which of the walkthrough's two travelling kinds this is, the fast short-spiked ball or the slow long-spiked one that turns at obstacles, is not settled.

51.name: Rolling stone
51.note: The grey cylinder that rolls slowly round a set course and can be jumped over. LEVEL 51 carries the game's first where the walkthrough says to jump the rolling stone, and LEVEL 52's four are the captivators it follows clockwise.

52.name: Captivator
52.note: A moving spiked thing that restarts the level on touch, with a direction in the field that varies. The game's first are LEVEL 22's seven, which the walkthrough says glide in front of the ball and are jumped past as they move away; which of its two travelling kinds this is, against type 50, is not settled.

53.name: Captivator, wandering
53.note: The blue hexagonal ball that shakes, then moves one square in a random direction. LEVEL 84 carries four where the walkthrough says to watch their shaking to tell which way they will go, and it has no direction field.

56.name: Captivator, bouncing
56.note: The corkscrew that bounces up and down: roll under it when up, jump it when down. LEVEL 45 carries six where the walkthrough says to roll under them when raised, and LEVEL 122's go up in sequence, which is what the four-valued field reads as.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#15.note: The walkthrough's maximum. The disc holds 3500 more, the twelve coins on the corners of the lowest ring: they and the four gems inside that ring cannot both be had, and the walkthrough takes the gems. The Japanese release removes the coins.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#18.note: The walkthrough's figure, which it marks with a question mark: it leaves one of the ten crumbling blocks, and counts the coin under the exit block that the Japanese release removes as unreachable. The disc holds 50 more.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#19.note: The developer object catalogue, shipped unchanged in nine of the ten worlds and never reached in play. One of nearly every object in the game stands on a flat floor: walk it in an emulator and each one names itself. `tools/kula_objlevel.py` writes the floor plan, and `tools/kula_warp.py --cheat` prints the emulator cheat that reaches it.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#7.note: The walkthrough's maximum. The disc holds 100 more, two of the five crumbling blocks, which the walkthrough's route leaves standing without saying so.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#13.note: The walkthrough's maximum. The Japanese release moves the world's hidden exit to this level.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#15.note: The walkthrough's maximum. The disc holds 1000 more, the two coins on top of the first platform, a face the walkthrough says cannot be reached; the Japanese release removes them.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#16.note: The walkthrough's maximum. The disc holds 750 more, a gold coin's worth that the walkthrough's route does not take and does not name.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#17.note: The walkthrough's maximum. The disc holds 250 more, a bronze coin's worth that the walkthrough's route does not take and does not name. This is the one arcade level rebuilt between the PAL and the NTSC release, and its thirty pickups are the only ones in the game without a pickup number.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#18.note: 160 of its 178 blocks are not part of the level at all. They lie flat on z=32, the floor of the lattice and 22 blocks below the playable structure, spelling VERY WELL DONE in block letters six blocks tall. The other 18 are a frame standing in the xz plane, and everything the level places, the start, the exit, four keys, eight bronze coins and four of an unnamed type, stands on its -y face, from where the lettering reads the right way round.
